items.title: Opponents of Iran's regime worry two weeks of bombing has backfired
items.description: When US and Israeli air strikes first tore through the skies over Iran, some regime opponents felt a rush of optimism. Two weeks later, that sense of hope is fading.

items.title: The US is no longer directing the war against Iran
items.description: If there ever was a strategy behind Donald Trump's decision to blow up the Middle East, it is lying in tatters as the second week of the Iran war draws to a close.

items.title: Why has the US attacked Iran's Kharg Island?
items.description: Donald Trump says the US has "obliterated" Iran's military assets on the island, but stopped short of attacking other infrastructure.

items.title: He risked his life at Bondi. But this Iranian refugee failed our character test
items.description: AB ran into danger during Bondi's terrorist attacks to save lives. Four months on, he faces deportation after failing Australia's refugee character test. His family is urging the Albanese government to reconsider.

items.title: Free daytime power: What the new offer means for Australian households
items.description: Australia's energy watchdog prepares to unveil new power price caps, which will include a tariff offering three hours of free electricity during the day.

items.title: Fresh twist in case of child molester and former international fugitive
items.description: There been a fresh twist in the long-running saga of child molester Charles Batham, with NSW authorities requesting his transfer from jail interstate to face new charges.

items.title: Homes inundated and locals banding together: NT flooding in pictures
items.description: Many regions across the Northern Territory were submerged by flooding this week. Here is some of the best footage from the extreme weather event, right across the Top End.

items.title: 'Astronomical' fares soar amid Middle East flight chaos
items.description: John McGuigan was due to go back to work weeks ago in Manchester. He's still stuck in Australia using up all his work leave entitlements due to the war in the Middle East.

items.title: Lawyers sharpen tactics after ICE arrests schoolboy on way to volleyball
items.description: The case of a US teen who was pulled over and detained on his way to volleyball training highlights ICE's tactics, and how lawyers are fighting back.

items.title: What will Australia's relaxed fuel standards mean for consumers at the pump?
items.description: The federal government's temporary easing of fuel standards will see 200 million litres of "dirty" fuel injected into the domestic market. Should drivers be worried?

items.title: Live: Tigers kick off season with demolition of Cowboys
items.description: The Wests Tigers start their 2026 season with a 44-16 win over the Cowboys before the Storm take on the Dragons and the Panthers face the Sharks in Bathurst. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Cats face Freo challenge, slick Bulldogs thrash lacklustre Giants
items.description: The Bulldogs maintain their unbeaten start to the season, hammering the Giants with a 21-goal performance at Docklands, as Geelong takes on Fremantle. Follow live.

items.title: Russell wins Shanghai sprint for Mercedes, Piastri finishes sixth
items.description: George Russell holds off the fast-starting Ferraris to win the Chinese Grand Prix sprint race, as Oscar Piastri finishes further back in the field.

items.title: Why experts are worried about the latest peptides trend
items.description: The latest wellness craze to take social media by storm is fuelling a growing grey market of injectable peptides in Australia, and it has experts worried.

items.title: Here's why Melburnians never fell for Kyle and Jackie O
items.description: You could argue Melbourne didn't warm to the the duo's shock jock style but I think the answer is much simpler.

items.title: At 102 years old, Dean Simes might be Australia's oldest tech-help guy
items.description: Dean Simes bought his first personal computer this century. Now, the centenarian wants to help other seniors understand the technology "you can't avoid".

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of 70s rock, Pixar and our national anthem
items.description: Every question has only two options: one is right and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: Rotating home owners boast of 360-degree views and energy benefits
items.description: They may be costly to build, but rotating homes are loved for the way they can move with the sun, capture breezes from any direction and make the most of the scenery around them.

items.title: Former spy chief says Bondi intelligence findings 'cannot wait'
items.description: Dennis Richardson calls for a second interim report from the royal commission into antisemitism, warning it would be "unacceptable" to leave findings about any intelligence failures that contributed to the Bondi terrorist attack until the end of the year.

items.title: First known image of Mountbatten-Windsor, Mandelson and Epstein released
items.description: An image appearing to show Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and the sacked UK ambassador to Washington, Peter Mandelson, with convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein has been uncovered in the latest document dump released by the US DOJ.

items.title: Gulf migrants say they are 'safe and happy' amid missile and drone attacks
items.description: For many South Asian migrants across the Gulf, keeping quiet about Iran's attacks ensures they're able to pay the bills and feed their families. But is leaving even an option?

items.title: Using email from wrong Stephen King was 'insulting', partner says
items.description: Bronwen Paterson spoke out about the devastation of her partner experiencing ramping in his final hours. Then, a government email bungle left her traumatised.

items.title: 'Bit of a dodgy move': Bluesfest ticketholders question cancellation timing
items.description: Festival revellers, who have spent thousands on the event, are angry and have been left wondering when organisers knew it was not viable.

items.title: Will a national weed listing help control buffel grass?
items.description: Traditional owners and scientists want buffel grass recognised as a Weed of National Significance, but the cattle industry opposes the move because it relies on the species for fodder.

items.title: 'What about us?' Iranians waiting years to receive asylum in Australia
items.description: Iranian refugees in Australia welcome Iran's footballers being granted asylum, but question why others remain stuck on a years' long waitlist for permanent residency.
